thread:
alex: Quick heads-up — I kicked off a lightweight role-binding audit against our prod identity index and found ~60 service-role bindings with zero principal activity in the last 180 days. Thinking we should run a deeper validation before pruning. infra-bot ran the initial scan.
infra-bot: Scan completed: 60 potential orphaned service-role bindings. Summary uploaded: https://internal/reports/role-audit/1933333333 (csv + JSON).
maria: Do we have a safe runbook for removing service role bindings? We need to avoid breaking scheduled batch jobs and CI agents.
alex: Proposed plan: 1) mark candidates with label `orphan-candidate` and try to resolve owners via owner-mapping. 2) attach a TTL tag `orphan-flag:14d` and do a dry-run removal to collect errors. 3) run a staged prune (canary) removing 5 bindings from low-risk projects, monitor for 48h. 4) if no issues, escalate to bulk removal with 7-day notice. Rollback via `infra rbac-restore`.
jen: @alex can you paste the query/command you used so I can run the same on staging?
alex: SQL I used (simplified):
```sql
SELECT binding_id, role, principals, last_seen
FROM iam_bindings
WHERE type = 'service'
  AND (last_seen IS NULL OR last_seen < now() - interval '180 days');
```
Also quick python check to confirm principal activity (pseudo):
```python
for b in bindings:
    for p in b.principals:
        last = get_last_activity(p)
        if last and last > cutoff:
            mark_active(b)
```
sam: Strong +1 for a canary. Suggest removing 5 at a time from non-critical projects and adding an alert: deployment error rate increase >2% or SLO latency spike -> immediate rollback.
maria: KMS caution: some service roles only appear inactive because they are used solely in KMS key policies. Before any deletion we should cross-check KMS key grants: `kms:ListKeyPolicies` and `kms:ListGrants`.
tara: Compliance request: ensure audit logs capture any deletion actions. CloudTrail retention must cover 90-day compliance window for this activity. Also tag any manual approval entries so we can produce evidence.
jen: I'll run the staging query and a matching KMS cross-check today. Will report back with a small sample. Ping me if you want me to handle owner notifications.
alex: I'll open an ops-runbooks ticket with the candidate list and add a cleanup checklist + rollback commands. Will add `infra rbac-restore <binding_id>` steps and KMS re-grant steps.
maria: Also add a step to update owners in the owner-mapping DB; some entries are stale and block automated notification.
sam: I'll draft the canary job and add a Prometheus alert: `rbac_prune_failures > 0` or error-rate spike > 2% -> postmortem and rollback.
alex: Great — let's sync tomorrow 10:00am to review staging results and decide go/no-go. If staging shows false positives, we'll widen the heuristics. :thumbsup:
jen: Sounds good, I'll post the staging sample in this thread when ready.
infra-bot: Reminder: automated dry-run scheduled at 1933333380 (will log all attempted removals to /var/log/rbac-dryrun/1933333333.log).
alex: Thanks everyone — will update the ticket and tag owners once we have the validated candidate list.
